title: GL Building as Lattice Functions
body_html:
GL Building as Lattice Functions

The extended building \(B(\operatorname{GL}(V))\) is identified with the set of lattice functions on \(V\), equivalently with splittable \(D\)-norms, as a \(\operatorname{GL}(V)\)-set. This identification is unique up to translation.

If \(x\in B(\operatorname{GL}(V))\) corresponds to \(L\), then \[ \operatorname{LieGL}(V)_{x,r}=\operatorname{LieGL}(V)_{L,r},\qquad \operatorname{GL}(V)_{x,r}=\operatorname{GL}(V)_{L,r}\quad(r>0), \] and \[ \operatorname{GL}(V)_x=\operatorname{GL}(V)_L. \]
proof_html: The paper cites the standard Bruhat-Tits and Moy-Prasad identification. On an apartment, a splittable norm is determined by the values of a splitting basis, and the Moy-Prasad lattice conditions are exactly the operator-shift conditions defining \(\operatorname{LieGL}(V)_{L,r}\) and \(\operatorname{GL}(V)_{L,r}\).
